title: One-dimensional arrays
sub: Worksheet for the 360° experience: Stock shelves
objectives: know how to create a list and read one item out of it by its index
understand how to traverse a list in order to total, count or compare its items
know how to add an item onto a list and how to take one out again
starter: The list shelf holds Nails, Screws, Bolts and Nuts, in that order. Write down what shelf[0], shelf[3] and len(shelf) each give, and the index of the last item.

stations.name: Making a list
stations.fact: The exam calls these arrays. Python calls them lists, and unlike an array they can grow and shrink.
stations.challenge: Which line must go above the loop that fills a list, and why?

exam: A loop over a list of six prices begins for i in range(1, 6). State which price is never looked at, and rewrite the line so that every price is included.
Write a program that reads 6 javelin throws in metres into a list, then prints the longest throw and the position it is stored at.
Write a program that holds a list of five club members, removes a name the user types in, then prints the list and how many members are left.
